facts.fact: Gavi's VaccinesWork reports that Djibouti faces the vagaries of medical follow-up kept on paper and a risk of information being lost along a paper care pathway, the second point attributed to WHO's representative; the statement is general, names no tier and no system, and is undated, so the publication date of 29 August 2024 is used.

systems.owner: Medyc, a private company; €100,000 from ACE Capital, selected late 2023
systems.tiers: direct to patients in Djibouti city: 1,200 people registered for teleconsultation; about a hundred diabetes patients monitored through a mobile application since 1 July 2024; remote reading of the CHU de Djibouti's radiology by specialists in Morocco; video follow-up of high-risk pregnancies and automated child-vaccine reminders for the Dar al Hanan hospital

systems.platform: Starlink terminal with a computer and solar panel
systems.owner: Medyc with the Ministry of Health
systems.tiers: three devices planned for the remotest places, operated by local nurses; planned, not installed, at 29 August 2024

note: One fact, and a weak one: the paper position is stated in general terms in the standfirst and in a paraphrase of WHO's representative, not as a statement about every tier; the parent should weigh whether it is a dated statement of absence. The rest of the article is a private telemedicine firm and a planned satellite pilot, both enabling; it describes no patient record held by a facility and no routine reporting system.
